title: True righteousness is infused, not humanly acquired
source_text: XV. Porro Justitia haec quae Deo tantopere placet, cuique vitam & gloriam aeter-nam pollicetur, multum ab humana & civili discrepat. Sed in eo praesertim, quod justitia humana industria & viribus humanis acquiritur. Constat enim habitibus vir-tutum moralium, quae crebro repetitis earundem actibus in anima paulatim forman-tur. Ad justitiam autem illam quam Deus gratam & acceptam habet humanae vires attingere non valent: nec quisquam ex se & propriis viribus, ad eam sese disponere & praeparare potest: sed, ut ex jam dictis satis evidens est, necesse est illam divi-nitus infundi, & in nostris animis coelesti gratia operante formari. Quandoquidem illi qui talem justitiam adipiscuntur, & Dei beneficio sancti justique evadunt, a Deo vivificari, regenerari, & de novo creari dicuntur. Cum ante essent in peccatis mortui, Joh. 3. 6. & ex carne geniti nihil essent nisi mera caro, Rom. 8. 8. in qua qui sunt Deo placere non possunt, sed sunt inimici Dei mente & operibus malis, Col. 1. 21.
pass_a_gloss: Further, this righteousness which so greatly pleases God, and to which he promises eternal life and glory, differs much from human and civil righteousness—especially in this, that human righteousness is acquired by industry and human powers. For it consists in habits of moral virtues which are gradually formed in the soul by frequently repeated acts of the same. But human powers cannot attain to that righteousness which God holds gracious and acceptable; nor can anyone of himself and by his own powers dispose and prepare himself for it: but, as is clear enough from what has already been said, it must be infused from above and formed in our souls by the working of heavenly grace. Since those who obtain such righteousness and by God's benefit become holy and just are said to be vivified, regenerated, and newly created by God—whereas before they were dead in sins (John 3:6) and, born of flesh, were nothing but mere flesh (Romans 8:8), in which those who are cannot please God but are enemies of God in mind and wicked works (Colossians 1:21).
pass_b_english: This God-pleasing justice differs from civil/human virtue gained by repeated acts.
It must be divinely infused; those who receive it are said to be vivified, regenerated, newly created.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1049.
